title: Ada changes her email: a natural key without cascade, with cascade, and a surrogate key

steps.note: round 1: customers keyed by email, orders point at the email.

steps.sql: UPDATE customers SET email = 'ada@lovelace.dev' WHERE email = 'ada@example.com'
steps.note: the key is referenced, and the foreign key says NO ACTION: three orders still point at the old email, so the update fails.

error.message: update or delete on table "customers" violates foreign key constraint "orders_customer_email_fkey" on table "orders"
error.detail: Key (email)=(ada@example.com) is still referenced from table "orders".

steps.sql: SELECT id, customer_email, total FROM orders ORDER BY id

steps.note: round 2: the same, with ON UPDATE CASCADE on the foreign key.

steps.sql: UPDATE customers SET email = 'ada@lovelace.dev' WHERE email = 'ada@example.com'
steps.note: one UPDATE on customers. the cascade rewrites every order that pointed at the old email.

steps.sql: SELECT id, customer_email, total FROM orders ORDER BY id
steps.note: three orders rewritten: three new row versions, three index entries, WAL for each.
round 3: a surrogate id is the key, the email is just a unique column.

steps.sql: UPDATE customers SET email = 'ada@lovelace.dev' WHERE email = 'ada@example.com'
steps.note: the email changes in one row.

steps.sql: SELECT id, customer_id, total FROM orders ORDER BY id
steps.note: orders didn't notice: they point at id 1, which never changes.
